items.capacity: AI research lab; manifesto authors and co-founders
items.fact: Inherent's own site (read directly) says it will 'collectively self-improve to discover new knowledge' and credits Tantum Collins, Edward Hughes, Louis Kirsch and Kaloyan Aleksiev as manifesto authors. Press reports describe its product as Faraday, an AI system for open-ended scientific discovery, and the company as a public benefit corporation.
items.quote: Inherent will collectively self-improve to discover new knowledge.
items.missing: Manifesto date; Faraday product page not read; company benchmark claims unverified.
items.notes: TechCrunch (read directly, dated 2026-08-22) calls Edward Hughes 'co-founder and chief scientist' and reports Inherent's claim that its agent beat larger Anthropic and OpenAI models at replicating research; that is the company's own claim. Kaloyan Aleksiev's earlier roles (Reka AI, Microsoft) are from tech.eu (read).

items.fact: GovAI's team page (read directly) says 'Tantum is CEO of Inherent.' Penguin Random House's author page (read directly) says he is 'currently the CEO of an AI research startup' without naming it. Companies House lists him only as director (see T6.8).
items.publisher: Centre for the Governance of AI (GovAI)
items.missing: Inherent's own statement of his title; start date; company or LinkedIn bio not read.
items.notes: Search snippet only (page not read): a directory bio says 'currently Chief Executive Officer at Inherent' (updated 2026-06-01); the directory's contact details suggest a possibly different company, so its identity is unconfirmed. CB Insights snippet names Olivier Grosjeanne as Inherent CTO. TNW photo caption reads 'CEO-Inherent' (LinkedIn credit), which is a caption, not a title statement.

items.capacity: Co-lead of $50m seed round, with Radical Ventures
items.fact: Index Ventures' own post (read directly, dated 2026-05-31) says it is proud 'to lead their $50m seed round, alongside Radical Ventures'. Tech.eu (2026-05-29) and TNW (2026-05-30) report the same co-lead, and the round size of $50m is confirmed; the UKTN headline says GBP 40m but its body says '$50m (GBP 37.2m)'.
items.quote: We're proud to stand with them to lead their $50m seed round, alongside Radical Ventures
items.missing: Closing date and per-investor amounts; investment documents; shareholder data for Inherent (no cap table read).
items.notes: A round-up search snippet (page not read) says Index led and Radical joined; Index's own post contradicts that, so Index's post is the stronger source. A tracker (page not read) lists the funding date as 2026-05-28. TNW says the company emerged 'on Wednesday', but tech.eu and UKTN date the announcement to Friday 2026-05-29.

items.capacity: Co-lead of $50m seed round, with Index Ventures
items.fact: Tech.eu (read directly, dated 2026-05-29) reports that the seed round was co-led by Index Ventures and Radical Ventures. Page not read for Radical's own post: the radical.vc URLs I tried returned 404; a search snippet quotes it as announcing 'our Seed investment in Inherent' and attributes it to partner Aaron Rosenberg.
items.quote: The $50m seed round in Inherent was co-led by Index Ventures and Radical Ventures.
items.missing: Radical's own announcement read directly; Radical fund and LP data; the brief's register facts (see notes).
items.notes: Brief's register facts not confirmed: a DSIT AI investor roundtable with Matt Clifford on 2023-10-25, and a 2026-03-05 meeting with the AI minister on the SovAI launch. My searches found no Radical entry for either. The gov.uk Technology Secretary AI roundtable page (read directly; undated in the text read, search summary says June 2023) lists 'Matt Clifford, ARIA' among attendees and no Radical Ventures attendee. The 2026 DSIT ministerial-meeting transparency file was not found.

items.fact: TNW (read directly, dated 2026-05-30) says 'Nvidia's venture arm NVentures also participated, alongside Ex/Ante, Metaplanet, Macroscopic Ventures, and Mythos Ventures.' No investor's own page was read for NVentures or the other four.
items.quote: Nvidia's venture arm NVentures also participated
items.missing: Investor-confirmed amounts and stakes; primary statements from NVentures, Ex/Ante, Metaplanet, Macroscopic and Mythos.
items.notes: A second round-up search snippet (page not read) lists the same participants.

items.fact: Index Ventures' own post (read directly, 2026-05-31) lists Matt Clifford CBE, who previously advised the Prime Minister on AI, as an advisor to the company. Tech.eu (read directly) says he 'is an advisor to Inherent' and was co-founder of Entrepreneurs First; UKTN (read directly) says the firm 'has been backed by major industry figures including Matt Clifford', the only source that frames him as a backer.
items.quote: Matt Clifford CBE, who previously advised the Prime Minister on AI, is an advisor
items.missing: Start date and terms of the advisory role; any equity (no cap table read); Clifford's own statement; Inherent's own adviser list (not read).
items.notes: Entrepreneur First: Clifford is described as co-founder of EF (tech.eu, read). No EF investment in Inherent found. A search snippet (page not read) says Clifford gave up running EF in December 2023 to focus on AI. TNW (read) says 'Ex-UK AI tsar Matt Clifford advises.'

items.capacity: Director and person with significant control; Oakwood Corporate Secretary Limited (registration 7038430) is secretary
items.fact: Companies House officers and PSC pages (read directly) list Tantum Stuart Collins as active director appointed 16 January 2026, and as the only active person with significant control, notified 16 January 2026. The same officers page lists Oakwood Corporate Secretary Limited as active secretary from the same date; the filing history shows two outstanding charges created 22 April 2026 (holder not shown in pages read), a CS01 on 29 June 2026, and an AA01 on 6 October 2026 shortening the first accounting period to 31 December 2026.
items.missing: Charge holders and terms (MR01 PDFs not opened); nature of control for the PSC (not read).
items.notes: Only two officers: Collins (director) and Oakwood (secretary); no resignations and no other directors. Companies House shows no CEO role for Collins. Oakwood Corporate Services Limited, an ACSP, verified Collins's identity on 13 January 2026. Registered office is 3rd Floor, 1 Ashley Road, Altrincham, Oakwood's address.

items.capacity: Research Scientist leading the Meta-Research team (GovAI); research lead, Meta-Research team (80,000 Hours); Principal for Research and Strategy (CSET); titles differ by source
items.fact: Penguin Random House (read directly) says 'Before joining government, he spent five years at Google DeepMind.' GovAI (read directly) says he worked at DeepMind 'as a Research Scientist, leading the Meta-Research team', and CSET (read directly) says he served as 'Principal for Research and Strategy at DeepMind'. The Index page (read) says 'after DeepMind, Tantum handled AI policy issues at the Biden White House'.
items.quote: Before joining government, he spent five years at Google DeepMind
items.missing: Exact start and end months at DeepMind; LinkedIn or DeepMind records not read.
items.notes: Co-authorship: 'Open Problems in Cooperative AI' (arXiv 2012.08630, submitted 15 Dec 2020, read directly) lists Allan Dafoe, Edward Hughes, Yoram Bachrach, Tantum Collins, Kevin R. McKee, Joel Z. Leibo, Kate Larson and Thore Graepel as authors. Demis Hassabis: not found. Two searches returned no source naming Collins together with Hassabis. PRH also lists him as coauthor of 'Team of Teams' and author of 'The Bitter Struggle'.

items.to: National Security Council, The White House (Biden administration)
items.capacity: Director for Technology and National Security
items.fact: Penguin Random House author page (read directly) says that as Director for Technology and National Security he 'handled AI issues at the National Security Council during the Biden administration'. The start year is approximate: the 80,000 Hours interview (published 2023-10-12, read directly) has him 'heading back in just a few weeks' to DC for 'another AI-focused policy role' and says he had 'not yet begun the role'. A ContactOut profile (search snippet, page not read) dates the NSC role July 2023 to January 2025, which conflicts with 'just a few weeks' in October 2023.
items.quote: handled AI issues at the National Security Council during the Biden administration.
items.missing: Official whitehouse.gov or NSC record (none found); exact start and end dates; confirmation that the 80,000 Hours 'AI-focused policy role' is the NSC role (inferred, not stated).
items.notes: Not the same post as Tarun Chhabra, Senior Director for Technology and National Security (search snippet on the 2021 transition team).

items.to: White House Office of Science and Technology Policy (OSTP)
items.capacity: Assistant Director for Technology Strategy (80,000 Hours, GovAI); Assistant Director for Technology Policy (Penguin Random House)
items.fact: 80,000 Hours (read directly, episode published 2023-10-12) says he 'was Assistant Director for Technology Strategy at the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy back in 2021 and 2022.' GovAI (read) gives the same title and says he oversaw 'a portfolio of issues related to AI and national security'; Penguin Random House gives 'Assistant Director for Technology Policy'.
items.quote: Assistant Director for Technology Strategy at the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy
items.missing: Official OSTP or whitehouse.gov record; exact start and end months; resolution of the Technology Strategy vs Technology Policy title conflict.
items.notes: In the interview, Collins says he left OSTP 'about six months ago' while the host says 2022; these do not agree, so the end year is the host's (2022). The 2021 start is the host's statement.
